title: Audit log: emit quantization profile change events (route enable/disable + profile ref diffs)
author: Jada Williams
description:
This PR adds structured audit log events for route-level quantization profile changes. We currently persist route config changes and have an audit log primitive, but quantization profile settings were not emitted with enough structure to support compliance exports, internal forensics, and Console change history views. This change emits explicit events when (a) quantization is enabled/disabled at the route level and (b) quantization_profile_ref changes (including transitions to/from "default"). Events include actor identity, tenant + route identifiers, the resolved change type, and a normalized diff payload so downstream exporters/SIEM can index reliably.

Scope:
- Emit new audit event types for quant profile changes in the route config write path.
- Include actor (user/service), auth context, tenant_id, route_id, and change diff fields.
- Normalize diff schema to support both API and Console changes (same event contract).
- Add unit tests + golden fixtures for event payloads.
- Add minimal docs for event fields for the audit exporter pipeline.

Non-goals:
- No approval workflow/2-person review gating (tracked separately).
- No retroactive backfill of historical route config changes.
- No changes to policy evaluation or runtime behavior.

Event contract (v1):
- event_name: one of quant_profile.enabled, quant_profile.disabled, quant_profile.ref_changed
- actor_type: user|service
- actor_id: stable id from auth token
- actor_email: populated for user actors when available
- tenant_id, route_id, route_name
- request_id + trace_id (when available)
- diff: normalized string fields (see tests) with old/new values for quant_profile_ref and enabled boolean

Notes:
- We intentionally log the user-supplied profile ref (e.g., "qp:llama3-70b:int8:v3" or "default") rather than the fully resolved runtime selection, to avoid ambiguity and keep the audit record tied to configuration intent.
- PII: actor_email is already present in other audit events; we follow the same redaction controls and retention.

Related:
- INT-9170: ensure audit exporter includes quant_profile_id/ref and route identifiers.
- PR-18496: Console backend route settings endpoints.
- PR-18566: Console changelog view (consumes these events).
commits: audit: add quant profile event types + schema constants
control-plane: emit quant_profile.enabled/disabled on route settings write
control-plane: emit quant_profile.ref_changed with normalized diff payload
audit-exporter: include quant_profile_ref fields in allowlist + docs
tests: add golden fixtures + unit tests for quant profile audit events
illustrative_snippet: New events are emitted from the route settings write handler after config validation succeeds and before persistence returns 200. For example: emitAuditEvent({ event_name: 'quant_profile.ref_changed', tenant_id, route_id, actor, diff: { field: 'quantization_profile_ref', old: prevRef ?? 'default', new: nextRef ?? 'default' } }). We also emit enabled/disabled events when the boolean toggle transitions.
conversation: Chloe Martin (review): Can we guarantee we only emit one event per request? If a user flips enabled=false and also clears ref in the same PATCH, are we emitting multiple events?

Jada Williams (author): Currently yes: we emit (1) enabled/disabled when the enabled flag transitions and (2) ref_changed when the ref changes. That matches other audit areas (multiple events per request) and is easier to query. I added request_id/trace_id so the exporter can correlate events.
Ethan Park (review): Please ensure we never log the resolved profile (post-policy) here. Audit should reflect config intent. Also, include route_name to make SIEM queries readable.
Jada Williams (author): Ack. Updated emitter to log only the user-specified quantization_profile_ref. Added route_name as a top-level field with route_id/tenant_id.

Naomi Feldman (security review): Actor fields: actor_email is ok but we should keep it optional for service actors and ensure redaction rules remain consistent. Also confirm RBAC failures do not emit events.

Jada Williams (author): actor_email is only present for actor_type=user; service actors include actor_id + service_name. RBAC failures short-circuit before any emit call; added a test asserting no audit events on 403.
Kevin Osei (audit export review): INT-9170 asks for quant_profile_id. Are we using id or ref? Exporter allowlist needs stable fields with clear semantics.

Jada Williams (author): We don’t have a stable numeric id at the config layer; we store a ref string (includes version). I updated naming to quant_profile_ref consistently across the event payload and exporter allowlist. Added docs entry clarifying it’s the configured ref, not resolved selection.
Chloe Martin (review): Nit: diff payload should be consistent strings; avoid nested objects in the proto so exporters don’t have to special-case. Can we flatten diff.* keys?
Jada Williams (author): Done. diff is now a set of string fields: diff_field, diff_old, diff_new, plus diff_enabled_old/new for the toggle path. Updated golden fixtures.
deployment_notes: No migration. Safe to deploy behind existing audit log pipeline. Verified in staging by toggling quantization on a test route and confirming three events: ref_changed, enabled, disabled (on revert). Exporter allowlist updated so fields appear in downstream exports.
release_notes: Internal: Audit log now records route-level quantization profile enable/disable and profile ref changes with actor/route metadata for compliance exports and Console change history.
